text:
It's basically a matter of how comfortable you and your relatives are with the risk. But if you really want to avoid having any issues and to practically guarantee a smooth arrival, then the invitation process is the only way to go. Personally, given the previous issues your brother had, as well as the change in circumstances with the war in Ukraine, I would absolutely go through the invitation process. Even if he brings all the additional evidence, they will may still want to hold and delay him while they review it. 

Also, for what it's worth, advance approval isn't strictly mandatory for people who are still in the gradual process on a temporary status - thousands of parents visit every year just with an ETA-IL. But there is always some risk of border issues for parents and relatives of those in the gradual process, and that risk can be higher (or lower) depending on their immigration profile - and so having a formal invitation is strongly recommended in some cases :)
